text:
li: Hi folks  I just opened my first PR for the metrics export (branch feat/metrics/export). Quick question: do we prefer a single squashed commit on merge or keep the incremental commits? Also any PR body template I should follow?

ana: Welcome li! For small features we usually squash on merge for a tidy main history. If the PR has helpful intermediate commits, keep them while iterating but squash before merging. Use the PR template and fill Testing, Rollout, and Backwards compatibility sections.

mike: Also, include the ticket reference (MET-56) at the top and a 1-line summary. If you touch public API surfaces, add product-approval label.

li: Cool. I ran `pre-commit` and got a handful of style fixes. Is it OK to push formatting changes as a separate commit?

ana: Yes, separate `chore(format): run black/ruff` commit is fine. Reviewers prefer functional changes separated from auto-formatting.

mike: CI-wise watch for ci/lint, ci/unit, ci/integration. If integration flakes, add the ci-flake label and ping #eng-sre.

li: What about rebasing policy? I rebased once and force-pushed to resolve conflicts. Should I avoid that?

ana: Force-push with `--force-with-lease` is fine before review. Once reviewers are assigned avoid rewrite unless you note it and re-request review.

pr-bot: Tip: comment `@pr-bot request-review` to re-trigger reviewer requests after a push.

li: Thanks. Anything else reviewers expect in the PR body?

mike: Short checklist in the body helps: 1) What changed and why, 2) How to test locally (commands), 3) Risk/rollback plan, 4) Migration notes. Example: "What: add metrics exporter to push to graphite. How: run `make dev` and POST sample payload. Risk: minimal, opt-in config"

li: Great, I'll update the PR with that and mark ready once tests pass. Thanks!

ana: Happy to pair on the rebase or CI failures if you want.

li: Appreciate it :pray:
